measurement: Model-judged qualified mechanisms absent from the finite independent reference bank.

task.title: Development: reversible list ordering
task.brief: A reading list supports manual reordering but currently requires dragging. Design a keyboard-accessible alternative for a list of 40 items.
constraints: Moving an item must be reversible until the page closes.
success_criteria: A user can move an item to a chosen position and undo it.

assignedCard.label: Archival provenance and original order
assignedCard.relation: Records gain meaning from who created them and how they were grouped in the originating activity. Preserving those relationships supports interpretation even when a new arrangement would look tidier. Description can expose access paths without silently replacing the evidence of the original organization.
assignedCard.boundary: An original order may be unknown, disrupted, or unsuitable for direct browsing. Do not invent one or treat historical organization as infallible; distinguish preserved evidence from a newly constructed access view.
assignedCard.source_fact: The National Archives describes provenance and preservation or restoration of original order, while allowing devised arrangements when order is lost.
assignedCard.source_note: Relation is an authored abstraction of the cited source, not a quotation. Boundary states limits on candidate transfer, not a tested product result.

actions.action: Add a keyboard-operated “Move to position” command.
actions.mechanism: An explicit destination moves an item anywhere in the 40-item list without repeated dragging or stepping.
actions.implementation: Open a labeled form from each item’s button; accept positions 1–40. On confirmation, reorder existing IDs, record undo, and retain focus.
actions.check: Using only the keyboard, move item 37 to position 2; verify its ID, announced position, focus, and successful undo.
actions.risk: Clarify that positions describe the final order; reject invalid entries.

j1.reason: A keyboard position form reorders existing IDs, records undo, and tests destination, focus, and reversal.

j2.reason: It uses a labeled keyboard position form to reorder existing IDs to a requested final position with undo and invalid-entry handling.

actions.action: Offer a keyboard move mode for nearby adjustments.
actions.mechanism: A focused item moves one place per arrow press, with an explicit commit or cancel.
actions.implementation: Enter through a “Reorder” button. Use arrows to preview order, Enter to commit one undoable change, and Escape to cancel; preserve IDs.
actions.check: Move an item three places, commit, then undo. Separately cancel a preview; verify unchanged order and focus. Test both list boundaries.
actions.risk: Intercept arrows only in move mode; announce instructions and position.

j1.reason: A keyboard-only preview mode groups arrow movements into one reversible commit and checks cancellation, focus, and boundaries.

j2.reason: Moving a focused item one place per arrow press with commit, cancel, undo, and ID preservation matches the incremental keyboard movement mechanism.

actions.action: Keep undo available throughout the page’s lifetime.
actions.mechanism: A page-scoped history restores earlier ID sequences rather than attempting to reverse drag coordinates or recreate items.
actions.implementation: Before every committed reorder, including dragging, save the ordered IDs. Provide a keyboard-accessible “Undo reorder” button; retain history across component remounts without expiry.
actions.check: Perform multiple moves through different controls, navigate within the page, then undo each; compare every restored sequence and ID set.
actions.risk: If deletion is supported, define reconciliation for IDs absent during undo.

j1.reason: Page-scoped ID snapshots and keyboard Undo preserve reversibility across remounts for every movement control.

j2.reason: Saving ordered IDs before every reorder and retaining keyboard undo across remounts satisfies the until-page-close undo mechanism.

actions.action: Add a keyboard-accessible “Move to position” control.
actions.mechanism: A numbered destination lets users relocate an item directly without dragging or repeated movement commands.
actions.implementation: Open a labeled form from each item; accept positions 1–40. On confirmation, reorder existing IDs, record undo, and restore item focus.
actions.check: Using only keyboard input, move item 37 to position 2; undo restores the exact previous ID sequence.
actions.risk: Explain that the number denotes the final position.

j1.reason: Numbered keyboard placement preserves IDs and records undo, with exact sequence restoration as its check.

j2.reason: A per-item keyboard form accepting positions 1–40 directly implements a final-position move and records undo while preserving IDs.

actions.action: Offer an explicit keyboard move mode.
actions.mechanism: Directional commands support incremental placement while keeping ordinary list navigation separate from reordering.
actions.implementation: Activate “Reorder” with Enter; use arrows to move and Home/End for boundaries. Enter commits one undoable move; Escape cancels. Announce position.
actions.check: Without a pointer, move an item through several positions, cancel, then repeat and commit; undo restores its starting position.
actions.risk: Scope shortcuts to move mode; test screen-reader interaction.

j1.reason: Scoped keyboard movement with commit and cancellation creates one undoable transaction rather than independently committed steps.

j2.reason: A scoped keyboard reorder mode uses directional movement and an undoable commit, which is the same incremental movement mechanism as move-up/down controls.

actions.action: Retain an accessible, page-lifetime undo history.
actions.mechanism: Saved ID sequences make every committed move reversible, rather than relying on a temporary notification.
actions.implementation: Before each move, push the ordered IDs onto an uncapped page-lifetime stack. Provide a persistent keyboard-focusable Undo button; restore order without regenerating IDs.
actions.check: Perform 50 moves, wait, then undo all 50. Every intermediate order must match its snapshot and retain all 40 IDs.
actions.risk: If items can be deleted, define restoration behavior explicitly.

j1.reason: Uncapped page-lifetime snapshots and persistent keyboard Undo preserve IDs and enable checking every restored order.

j2.reason: Saving ordered IDs on an uncapped page-lifetime stack with a keyboard Undo button matches the retained undo-history mechanism.

actions.action: Add a keyboard-accessible “Move to position” control.
actions.mechanism: Direct position entry avoids traversing up to 39 items to reach a chosen destination.
actions.implementation: Give each item a button opening a labeled integer input, 1–40. Enter commits through the undo journal; Escape cancels.
actions.check: Using only the keyboard, move item 37 to position 2, undo, and verify the exact original ID sequence.
actions.risk: Clarify that the number means position after moving.

j1.reason: Direct keyboard position entry uses an undo journal and checks restoration of the exact ID sequence.

j2.reason: A labeled integer input moves an item to a specified final position through the undo journal using only the keyboard.

actions.action: Offer an explicit keyboard reorder mode.
actions.mechanism: Arrow-key movement lets users adjust placement while retaining context among neighboring reading-list items.
actions.implementation: Activate an item’s “Reorder” button; arrows adjust a preview, Enter commits through the undo journal, and Escape cancels. Announce positions and retain focus.
actions.check: Without a pointer, move position 20 to 23 and undo. Verify announcements, retained focus, and unchanged item IDs.
actions.risk: Capture arrows only during reorder mode; provide visible instructions.

j1.reason: Arrow-key previews with explicit commit or cancellation differ operationally from separately committed step buttons.

j2.reason: Arrow-key preview and commit is a keyboard-only incremental reorder mechanism with undo, focus, announcements, and preserved IDs.

actions.action: Keep an undo journal until page close.
actions.mechanism: Retained order snapshots make every committed move reversible, rather than expiring reversal after a short notification.
actions.implementation: Before each commit, append the ID sequence to an uncapped page-session journal. Provide persistent keyboard-operable Undo; restore ordering without regenerating IDs.
actions.check: Commit 100 moves, dismiss notifications, then undo all 100. Compare every restored sequence with its snapshot and verify ID preservation.
actions.risk: Deletion or concurrent updates require explicit reconciliation before restoring snapshots.

j1.reason: A nonexpiring ID-sequence journal keeps committed moves reversible until page closure and checks one hundred reversals.

j2.reason: An uncapped page-session journal of ID sequences provides persistent undo until page close and avoids regenerating items.

actions.action: Add a keyboard-operated “Move to position” command.
actions.mechanism: An explicit destination moves any item without dragging or repeatedly stepping through forty positions.
actions.implementation: Give each item a button opening a labeled integer field, accepting 1–40. Commit by splicing its existing ID into the requested final position.
actions.check: Using only Tab, typing, and Enter, move item 37 to position 2; verify all forty IDs remain unchanged.
actions.risk: Clearly label positions as one-based; reject invalid input.

j1.reason: Keyboard numeric placement preserves existing IDs and specifies a concrete check, although undo history must be supplied separately.

j2.reason: The direct keyboard position entry preserves IDs, but it omits any undo/history behavior required by the reversibility constraint.

actions.action: Offer “Move before or after another item.”
actions.mechanism: A named destination lets users choose placement without knowing the target’s numerical position.
actions.implementation: Provide keyboard-accessible target and before/after selectors. Exclude the moving item; resolve the target by ID after removing the source from the order.
actions.check: Move an item before and after targets on either side; verify adjacent placement and an unchanged ID set.
actions.risk: Disambiguate duplicate titles with their current positions.

j1.reason: Keyboard before/after selectors resolve destinations by ID and test adjacency; page-lifetime undo remains a separate requirement.

j2.reason: The before/after target picker is implementable and ID-based, but it does not specify undo despite the reversibility constraint.

actions.action: Keep every committed move undoable throughout the page.
actions.mechanism: A page-lifetime history restores prior ID sequences rather than attempting potentially ambiguous inverse movements.
actions.implementation: Before either move command commits, push the current ID order onto an uncapped session stack. Provide a keyboard-accessible Undo button; never expire entries by timer.
actions.check: Perform fifty mixed moves, wait, then undo all fifty; require exact restoration of the starting sequence.
actions.risk: Other list mutations require an explicit compatible history policy.

j1.reason: An uncapped page-lifetime snapshot stack supports keyboard reversal and checks exact restoration after fifty moves.

j2.reason: Pushing current ID order before each committed move and retaining a nonexpiring Undo button implements page-lifetime reversibility.

actions.action: Preserve focus and announce each ordering change.
actions.mechanism: Stable focus and spoken status make committed moves and reversals observable without a pointer or visual tracking.
actions.implementation: Key rendered items by existing IDs. After moving or undoing, focus the affected item’s move button and announce its title and final position through a polite live region.
actions.check: With keyboard and screen reader, move and undo an item; verify focus follows its ID and each resulting position is announced.
actions.risk: Rerendering must not duplicate announcements or reset focus.

j1.reason: ID-keyed rendering, item-associated focus, and polite announcements make moves and undo observable to keyboard and screen-reader users.

j2.reason: It preserves ID-keyed focus and announces move/undo results, matching the focus-and-live-region accessibility mechanism without requiring a pointer.

actions.action: Make ordering an atomic ID-only operation
actions.mechanism: Separating item identity from position prevents reordering and undo from recreating items or losing records.
actions.implementation: Store order as an ID array alongside unchanged item records. Route every movement control through one validated remove-and-insert operation that records history before committing.
actions.check: Test all 1,600 source/destination pairs: retain the same 40 unique IDs, reach the requested position, and restore exact order on undo.
actions.risk: Destination indexing must refer to the final list.

actions.action: Preserve focus and announce completed moves
actions.mechanism: Stable focus and spoken position feedback keep keyboard and screen-reader users oriented after list changes.
actions.implementation: Key rendered rows by item ID. After movement, retain focus on that item’s control; announce its title and new position through a polite live region.
actions.check: Move a focused item from 40 to 1, then undo. Verify focus remains associated with that item and both positions are announced.
actions.risk: Overly frequent announcements can overwhelm repeated single-step moves.

actions.action: Offer placement before or after another item
actions.mechanism: Choosing a neighboring title lets users express a destination without knowing its position number.
actions.implementation: Provide a keyboard-operable destination picker and Before/After choice. Exclude the moving item; distinguish duplicate titles with their current positions.
actions.check: Place item 40 before item 2 and then after item 20 without a pointer; verify adjacency each time.
actions.risk: Long or duplicate titles can make destinations ambiguous.

actions.action: Provide one-step movement controls
actions.mechanism: Move up and Move down buttons support small adjustments without dragging or entering a destination.
actions.implementation: Expose native buttons in the focused item’s move panel. Keep focus on the activated control across updates; record each successful move separately.
actions.check: Move an item up three times using the keyboard, then undo three times; verify the exact starting order.
actions.risk: Boundary controls must explain unavailable moves without unexpectedly losing focus.

actions.action: Add a keyboard-operated “Move to position” control
actions.mechanism: An exact destination avoids repeated dragging or stepping through a 40-item list.
actions.implementation: Give each item a keyboard-accessible Move button. Open a labeled position field accepting integers 1–40; Enter applies, Escape cancels.
actions.check: Using only the keyboard, move item 37 to position 4. Reject blank, fractional, and out-of-range values without changing order.
actions.risk: Clarify that the number specifies the final position.

actions.action: Reorder IDs without recreating items
actions.mechanism: Separating item records from their ordered ID sequence preserves identity through movement, undo, and rendering.
actions.implementation: Keep records keyed by existing IDs. Implement moves as remove-and-insert operations on the ID sequence; use those IDs as rendering keys.
actions.check: For every source/destination pair, verify unchanged ID membership and count; undo must restore the exact sequence and retain item-local state.
actions.risk: Regenerating IDs or using position-based keys can silently replace item state.

actions.action: Retain undo history until page closure
actions.mechanism: An ordered history preserves every committed reorder, rather than only the latest move or a temporary notification.
actions.implementation: Store immutable before/after ID sequences and a history cursor in page-lifetime state. Provide persistent Undo/Redo buttons; do not expire or cap undo entries.
actions.check: Perform 100 moves, navigate within the application, then undo every move without closing the page; verify the initial order.
actions.risk: A new move after undo should explicitly discard the redo branch.

actions.action: Preserve focus and announce completed moves
actions.mechanism: Stable focus and concise status announcements make keyboard moves and reversals understandable without visual tracking.
actions.implementation: After applying or undoing, retain focus on the initiating control or restore it to the moved item’s button. Announce title and resulting position through a polite live region.
actions.check: With keyboard and screen reader, move and undo an item; confirm predictable focus and one accurate announcement per operation.
actions.risk: Avoid announcing the entire 40-item list after each change.

actions.action: Offer a numbered destination
actions.mechanism: A keyboard-operated position form moves an item directly to any final position from 1 through 40.
actions.implementation: Add a “Move” button opening a labeled numeric field and Apply/Cancel buttons. Define the entered number as the final position.
actions.check: Using only the keyboard, move item 37 to position 4; verify its position, then undo and verify the original order.
actions.risk: Reject invalid numbers without closing the form or changing order.

actions.action: Provide keyboard move-up and move-down buttons
actions.mechanism: Single-step movement supports nearby adjustments without opening a destination dialog or remembering keyboard shortcuts.
actions.implementation: Add labeled Move up and Move down buttons to each item’s controls. Keep focus on the activated control; make boundary actions unavailable.
actions.check: Move an item upward three places using only keyboard activation, then undo all three moves to restore its starting position.
actions.risk: Forty-item traversal remains tedious; retain direct destination controls.

actions.action: Keep undo history until the page closes
actions.mechanism: A page-lifetime history makes every completed move reversible, including moves made through different controls.
actions.implementation: Before each committed move, append the ordered ID array to an untruncated history stack. Provide a persistent, keyboard-accessible Undo button restoring the latest snapshot.
actions.check: Perform 100 mixed moves, dismiss every notification, then undo 100 times; require exact restoration of the original order.
actions.risk: Do not expire history with notifications or component unmounts.

actions.action: Offer placement before or after another item
actions.mechanism: Choosing a neighboring title avoids requiring users to know the destination’s number.
actions.implementation: Provide native selectors for Before/After and destination item, excluding the moving item. Disambiguate duplicate titles with current positions; commit through shared move history.
actions.check: Place an item after a duplicate-titled destination using only the keyboard; verify the selected neighbor and successful undo.
actions.risk: Long title selectors need readable, unambiguous option labels.

task.title: Development: temporary cache
task.brief: A small service caches public records for at most five minutes. A slow source can time out.
constraints: An expired record cannot be labeled fresh.
success_criteria: An outage has an explicit response and eviction behavior.

assignedCard.label: Cartographic generalization
assignedCard.relation: A representation for a smaller viewing scale selects, simplifies, or combines details so the remaining structure is legible. What is shown depends on the purpose and available space. A compact view is a deliberate representation of a richer source, not evidence that omitted features do not exist.
assignedCard.boundary: Simplification can erase distinctions that matter for another task. Keep access to the detailed source and choose what to retain according to the user's question rather than visual neatness alone.
assignedCard.source_fact: USGS describes map generalization as reducing detail and selecting appropriate content for a given scale.
assignedCard.source_note: Relation is an authored abstraction of the cited source, not a quotation. Boundary states limits on candidate transfer, not a tested product result.

actions.action: Enforce five-minute expiry and 100-record capacity.
actions.mechanism: Monotonic expiry controls freshness; expired-first, then least-recently-used eviction bounds the cache.
actions.implementation: Admit only allowlisted public fields from public sources. Set expiry at fetch start plus 300 seconds; atomically evict before insertion.
actions.check: With a fake clock, verify expiry at 300 seconds, including during outages. Insert 101 keys; assert at most 100 records.
actions.risk: Slow fetches shorten usable lifetime; discard responses already expired.

j1.reason: Fetch-start expiry and atomic expired-first eviction implement the five-minute and 100-record bounds with boundary tests.

j2.reason: It enforces fetch-start five-minute freshness, public-field admission, and expired-first/LRU capacity bounding.

actions.action: Return an explicit error when the source times out.
actions.mechanism: A fixed source deadline prevents indefinite waiting; failures never renew records or replace them with cached errors.
actions.implementation: Set a configurable fetch deadline. On timeout, cancel retrieval and return HTTP 503 with code source_timeout. Remove any expired entry; preserve unexpired entries.
actions.check: Simulate a hanging source. Verify timely 503, unchanged expiration timestamps, expired-entry removal, and no error-record insertion.
actions.risk: Cancellation must also stop underlying network work.

j1.reason: A cancelable fetch deadline produces explicit 503 errors while removing expired entries and preserving valid deadlines.

j2.reason: A bounded source deadline returns an explicit source_timeout and removes expired entries without inserting error records.

actions.action: Merge concurrent misses for the same record.
actions.mechanism: One in-flight fetch per key prevents duplicate source requests; bounded admission limits outage-related request buildup.
actions.implementation: Maintain an in-flight promise map capped at a configured size. Join existing fetches; reject excess distinct misses with 503 cache_busy. Remove promises on completion.
actions.check: Send concurrent requests for one missing key: observe one source call. Force timeout; verify shared errors and an empty promise map.
actions.risk: Bound waiters too; shared fetches otherwise accumulate callers.

j1.reason: A capped in-flight map coalesces duplicate misses and explicitly rejects excess distinct work, with cleanup checks.

j2.reason: A bounded in-flight promise map coalesces duplicate misses and rejects excess pending work.

actions.action: Temporarily stop source calls after repeated failures.
actions.mechanism: A circuit breaker makes sustained outages explicit while still serving cached records whose original expiry has not passed.
actions.implementation: After a configured consecutive-failure threshold, reject misses with 503 source_unavailable during cooldown. Then allow one probe; never extend TTL or suspend eviction.
actions.check: Force the threshold failures; verify no source calls during cooldown, expired-record eviction, one recovery probe, and resumed fetching after success.
actions.risk: Long cooldowns delay recovery; short cooldowns repeatedly probe outages.

j1.reason: Failure-triggered cooldown and a single recovery probe make outages explicit without extending TTL or suspending eviction.

j2.reason: Circuit breaker explicitly handles outages while serving only unexpired cache hits and preserving TTL/eviction rules.

actions.action: Expire records strictly and return explicit outage errors.
actions.mechanism: A fixed deadline prevents reads or source failures from extending a record’s freshness.
actions.implementation: Set monotonic expiry to insertion time plus 300 seconds, shortened by any source expiry. Delete expired entries before lookup; return 503 with source_timeout when retrieval times out.
actions.check: With a fake clock and stalled source, verify the expiry-boundary request returns 503 and removes the record.
actions.risk: Strict expiry sacrifices availability during source outages.

j1.reason: A fixed five-minute residence deadline and read-time deletion prevent expired hits, with explicit timeout errors.

j2.reason: Strict expiry plus source_timeout ensures expired records are removed rather than served during a stalled source.

actions.action: Enforce capacity with reserved slots and LRU eviction.
actions.mechanism: Atomic slot accounting bounds retained records, including refresh candidates, while eviction prioritizes expired entries.
actions.implementation: Use 100 slots. Reserve a slot before materializing a fetched record; evict expired entries, then least-recently-used entries. Release reservations on timeout; never extend existing expiry.
actions.check: Run concurrent requests for 150 keys during intermittent timeouts; assert occupied plus reserved slots never exceeds 100.
actions.risk: Reservations can evict useful records before unsuccessful fetches.

j1.reason: Atomic accounting of occupied and reserved slots enforces the 100-record limit under concurrent fetches.

j2.reason: Slot reservations include incoming work so occupied plus reserved records never exceed the 100-record cap.

actions.action: Coalesce retrievals and bound source waiting.
actions.mechanism: One retrieval per key prevents duplicate refreshes; a circuit breaker suppresses repeated calls during an outage.
actions.implementation: Share in-flight requests by key with a two-second deadline. After five consecutive failures, open the breaker for ten seconds, then permit one probe. Serve only unexpired hits; otherwise return 503.
actions.check: Issue 50 same-key misses against a stalled source: verify one call, bounded waits, and no expired response.
actions.risk: Breaker thresholds may reject requests during brief recoveries.

j1.reason: Per-key sharing and a timed circuit breaker jointly reduce outage calls, with bounded waits and an expired-response check.

j2.reason: It combines per-key request coalescing, bounded fetch time, and a circuit breaker while serving only unexpired hits.

actions.action: Admit only explicitly approved public record fields.
actions.mechanism: A public-only upstream projection prevents unnecessary or private fields from entering the cache.
actions.implementation: Request an allowlisted public schema from a public-only source endpoint. Validate before insertion; reject unexpected fields without logging payloads. Return 502 for rejected responses and release reserved slots.
actions.check: Inject an unexpected sensitive field; verify rejection, no cache insertion, reservation release, and no payload in logs.
actions.risk: Field allowlists cannot detect private values inside approved fields.

j1.reason: Public-only sourcing and pre-insertion schema validation address private-data exclusion, with rejection and reservation-release checks.

j2.reason: Approved public endpoints and schema validation prevent unexpected private fields from entering cache or logs.

actions.action: Delete expired records before serving requests
actions.mechanism: A monotonic five-minute deadline determines freshness; source failures never extend retention.
actions.implementation: Stamp successful insertions with expiry. Schedule deletion and recheck expiry on every read. Return 503 when an expired record cannot be replaced.
actions.check: With a fake clock and timed-out source, requests at five minutes return 503; the expired record is absent.
actions.risk: Scheduler delays require read-time enforcement, not timer-only freshness checks.

j1.reason: Scheduled deletion backed by read-time monotonic expiry checks prevents expired records being served during outages.

j2.reason: Read-time monotonic expiry deletion prevents expired records from being served fresh, including during source failure.

actions.action: Make capacity enforcement atomic
actions.mechanism: A single admission lock prevents concurrent insertions from exceeding the 100-record cache limit.
actions.implementation: Under the lock, remove expired entries, then evict the least recently used entry before inserting at capacity. Failed fetches trigger no capacity eviction.
actions.check: Race 150 distinct successful fetches: occupancy never exceeds 100. During failure-only traffic, unexpired entries remain until their deadlines.
actions.risk: Least-recently-used eviction can discard valuable records during sequential scans.

j1.reason: Locked eviction before insertion bounds cache occupancy at 100 without evicting valid entries for failed fetches.

j2.reason: A single admission lock with expired-first then LRU eviction enforces the 100-record memory limit.

actions.action: Bound source waits and suppress repeated failures
actions.mechanism: Timeouts and a circuit breaker turn a slow-source outage into predictable, explicit responses.
actions.implementation: Set a source timeout and failure threshold. While the breaker is open, serve only unexpired hits; return 503 with Retry-After for misses. Permit one recovery probe.
actions.check: Inject sustained timeouts: misses finish within the configured timeout, open-state requests skip fetching, and expiration deletion continues.
actions.risk: An excessive cooldown delays detection of source recovery.

j1.reason: Bounded source calls and a tested cooldown make outages explicit while preserving expiry deletion.

j2.reason: Source timeouts and an open breaker give explicit outage responses while preserving unexpired-hit serving and expiry deletion.

actions.action: Cache only an approved public-record projection
actions.mechanism: An explicit field allowlist excludes private data rather than trusting entire source payloads.
actions.implementation: Request only approved public fields from a public-only endpoint; validate before admission. Reject unexpected fields without logging payloads. Return 502 if no valid cached record exists.
actions.check: Inject an unexpected sensitive field: no payload is cached, returned, or logged, and an existing unexpired record remains unchanged.
actions.risk: Projection may omit distinctions callers require; document the response schema.

j1.reason: Public-source projection and rejection before admission enforce the no-private-data boundary, with a sensitive-field injection check.

j2.reason: A public-only projection and validation reject unexpected sensitive fields before cache admission or logging.

actions.action: Delete expired records and report source failures explicitly
actions.mechanism: Hard expiry prevents old records from appearing fresh; source failure never extends retention.
actions.implementation: Assign a monotonic expiry no later than 300 seconds after fetch starts. Delete on expiry and before reads. On refresh timeout, return 503 with source_timeout.
actions.check: With a fake clock and stalled source, verify expiration deletes the record, returns no cached payload, and produces 503.
actions.risk: Strict expiration sacrifices availability during outages.

j1.reason: Fetch-start deadlines and deletion before reads enforce five-minute expiry, with explicit timeout responses verified using a fake clock.

j2.reason: It combines monotonic hard expiry with explicit timeout failure and deletion of expired records.

actions.action: Bound admission to 100 public records
actions.mechanism: Atomic admission couples a public-field allowlist with deterministic least-recently-used eviction.
actions.implementation: Fetch only approved public endpoints and fields. Under one cache lock, purge expired entries, then evict the least-recently-used record before inserting at capacity.
actions.check: Insert 101 distinct records concurrently; assert occupancy never exceeds 100 and the expected victim disappears. Verify forbidden fields never enter cache or logs.
actions.risk: An incorrect allowlist can admit sensitive fields.

j1.reason: Locked expired-first LRU admission enforces 100 cached records, supplemented by public-field restrictions and concurrency checks.

j2.reason: Atomic expired-first/LRU admission enforces the 100-record cap while public-field allowlisting addresses private-data exclusion.

actions.action: Merge duplicate fetches and bound source work
actions.mechanism: One in-flight fetch per key prevents duplicate refreshes; deadlines bound waiting during source stalls.
actions.implementation: Share each key's fetch promise. Set a two-second source deadline and a global concurrency limit; reject excess uncached requests with 503 busy. Remove completed promises.
actions.check: Send simultaneous requests for one missing key; observe one source call. Stall it; verify all waiters finish and its promise is removed.
actions.risk: Shared fetch failures affect every waiting request.

j1.reason: Shared per-key promises, concurrency admission, and deadlines bound source work with observable stall tests.

j2.reason: Shared per-key fetches plus deadlines and a global concurrency limit bound duplicate and stalled source work.

actions.action: Temporarily stop calls to a failing source
actions.mechanism: A circuit breaker makes outage handling explicit without changing freshness or eviction rules.
actions.implementation: After three consecutive source timeouts, open for 30 seconds. Serve only unexpired hits; return 503 source_unavailable for misses. Continue expiry deletion; allow one recovery probe.
actions.check: Force three timeouts; verify misses make no source calls during cooldown, expired entries disappear, and a successful probe closes the breaker.
actions.risk: Cooldown can delay detection of source recovery.

j1.reason: A timed circuit opening suppresses outage calls while unexpired hits and ongoing expiry deletion remain available.

j2.reason: The circuit breaker stops repeated calls during outage, returns explicit 503 misses, and continues normal expiry deletion.

actions.action: Cap all resident records at 100
actions.mechanism: Slot reservations include cached records and incoming records, preventing concurrent fetches from exceeding capacity.
actions.implementation: Reserve a slot before fetching. Remove expired entries first, then least-recently-used entries. If every slot is reserved, reject new fetches explicitly.
actions.check: Run concurrent requests for 150 distinct records; assert occupied plus reserved slots never exceeds 100 and eviction order matches policy.
actions.risk: Counting incoming records reduces available cache capacity.

actions.action: Pause source calls after repeated failures.
actions.mechanism: A circuit breaker makes sustained outages explicit while preserving access to records that remain unexpired.
actions.implementation: After a configured failure threshold, open the circuit for a bounded cooldown. Serve valid hits; return 503 source_unavailable for misses. Permit one recovery probe.
actions.check: Force threshold failures, confirm no source calls during cooldown, then recover the source and verify one successful probe restores fetching.
actions.risk: Cooldown delays recovery detection; expiry and eviction rules must remain unchanged.

actions.action: Restrict ingestion to verified public fields
actions.mechanism: An explicit source and schema allowlist prevents private payloads from entering the cache.
actions.implementation: Use only approved public endpoints without user credentials. Disable redirects and raw-body logging. Stream allowed fields; reject unknown schemas and oversized responses.
actions.check: Inject forbidden fields, redirects, and oversized bodies; verify rejection without cache insertion, response disclosure, or payload logging.
actions.risk: Field filtering cannot establish whether a source is public.

actions.action: Enforce expiration independently of cleanup.
actions.mechanism: Read-time deadline checks prevent expired records being labeled fresh, even when background cleanup runs late.
actions.implementation: Stamp each fetch with monotonic start time; expire by start plus 300 seconds, or earlier source expiry. Delete expired entries before serving.
actions.check: With a fake clock, reads immediately before expiry succeed; reads at or after expiry miss, including during outages.
actions.risk: Starting freshness at fetch initiation shortens useful cache lifetime.

actions.action: Reject nonpublic data before cache admission.
actions.mechanism: An explicit public-data boundary prevents credentials, private fields, and personalized responses from entering the cache or diagnostics.
actions.implementation: Fetch only approved public endpoints without user credentials. Validate a public-field allowlist, reject unexpected fields, and disable request-body and response-body logging.
actions.check: Inject an unexpected sensitive field and a credential-bearing request; verify rejection and absence from cache, logs, and error responses.
actions.risk: Field validation alone cannot establish that a source is public.

actions.action: Enforce a hard five-minute expiry
actions.mechanism: Monotonic deadlines prevent clock changes or repeated reads from extending freshness.
actions.implementation: Set expiry to fetch-start time plus 300 seconds. Purge at expiry and before reads; discard responses arriving after their deadline.
actions.check: With a fake clock, verify a record is unavailable at exactly 300 seconds, including after repeated reads and wall-clock changes.
actions.risk: Conservative timing shortens useful lifetime for slow fetches.

actions.action: Expose cache age and failure state
actions.mechanism: Explicit response metadata distinguishes valid cached records from source failures and downstream stale copies.
actions.implementation: Return fetched_at, expires_at, and cache status with successful records. Set Cache-Control: no-store on responses. Use stable machine-readable error codes without record bodies.
actions.check: Inspect hit, miss, timeout, and circuit-open responses; confirm accurate timestamps, distinct error codes, and no freshness label on failures.
actions.risk: Clients may ignore metadata; server-side expiry remains authoritative.

actions.action: Coalesce duplicate fetches and bound pending work.
actions.mechanism: One source fetch per key prevents duplicate requests; bounded admission prevents outage-driven accumulation of pending work.
actions.implementation: Maintain a bounded map of in-flight promises. Join existing fetches; reject excess distinct-key fetches with 503 busy. Remove promises on every completion path.
actions.check: Send simultaneous misses for one key: observe one source call. Hang distinct-key requests and verify the configured pending-work limit holds.
actions.risk: Waiters need independent cancellation without canceling their shared fetch.

actions.action: Make timeout and outage responses explicit.
actions.mechanism: A bounded source request produces a documented unavailable response rather than an expired record or indefinite wait.
actions.implementation: Set a configurable source deadline. On timeout, cancel the fetch and return 503 with source_timeout. Delete expired entries; retain unexpired entries until their deadlines.
actions.check: Simulate a hanging source: misses return 503 within the configured deadline and scheduling tolerance; expired records are never returned.
actions.risk: An overly short deadline rejects recoverable slow requests.

actions.action: Stop repeatedly calling a failing source
actions.mechanism: A circuit breaker temporarily rejects misses while allowing still-valid cache hits.
actions.implementation: After three consecutive source failures, open the circuit for 30 seconds. Return 503 with Retry-After; then allow one probe. Never modify cache deadlines.
actions.check: During an induced outage, verify no source calls occur while open, only one recovery probe runs, and expiry continues normally.
actions.risk: Recovery can remain undetected until the next probe.

actions.action: Coalesce simultaneous requests for one record
actions.mechanism: One bounded fetch per key avoids duplicate source calls and competing cache writes.
actions.implementation: Maintain a bounded in-flight key map. Share fetch results among waiters; clear entries on completion. Reject late writes using fetch-generation tokens.
actions.check: Issue 50 simultaneous misses for one key; observe one source call. Deliver a timed-out result late and verify no insertion.
actions.risk: Waiter counts also need limits to bound metadata.

actions.action: Prevent late fetches from resurrecting records.
actions.mechanism: Fetch-generation checks block obsolete or canceled completions from overwriting newer data or recreating entries after invalidation.
actions.implementation: Give each admitted fetch a generation token. Commit only if its token remains current, its request remains active, and its original expiry deadline has not passed.
actions.check: Complete a canceled fetch after a newer successful fetch; verify no overwrite. Complete another after its deadline; verify no cache insertion.
actions.risk: Generation bookkeeping must be bounded and removed when no longer needed.

actions.action: Refresh active records before their expiry
actions.mechanism: Early refresh can obtain a replacement before a slow source makes the existing record unavailable.
actions.implementation: For recently accessed entries, schedule refresh between 240 and 270 seconds. Reserve replacement capacity and coalesce requests. Failures never extend the old deadline.
actions.check: Delay refresh beyond the old expiry; verify the old record disappears on time and replacement admission respects the 100-record limit.
actions.risk: Refresh traffic may worsen source overload; honor the circuit breaker.

actions.action: Define timeout responses and outage eviction
actions.mechanism: Bounded source waits produce explicit failures without treating expired records as usable cache hits.
actions.implementation: Set a two-second source timeout. Return 504 with source_timeout; return 503 for unavailable sources. Retain unexpired entries only until their original expiry.
actions.check: Simulate a hanging source: fresh hits succeed, misses return 504, and expired entries are removed rather than served.
actions.risk: Two seconds is an initial policy requiring operational review.

actions.action: Bound storage with deterministic eviction.
actions.mechanism: Atomic admission keeps the cache within 100 records while preserving useful entries during source failures.
actions.implementation: Under one lock, remove expired entries, then evict the least recently used entry only when admitting a successful new record into a full cache.
actions.check: Insert 101 distinct records and verify the expected eviction. Concurrent insertions never exceed 100 entries; failed fetches never evict unexpired entries.
actions.risk: Large individual records still require a separate byte limit.

task.title: Development: shared-room checkout
task.brief: A club lends a shared meeting room key between two volunteers. The current chat thread makes the location unclear.
constraints: A handoff must record its time.
success_criteria: The current holder and unresolved handoffs can be identified.

assignedCard.label: Comparator hysteresis
assignedCard.relation: A state changes only when an input crosses an upper boundary in one direction or a lower boundary in the other. Between those boundaries it retains the preceding state. Separating the two transitions prevents small fluctuations around one threshold from repeatedly toggling the output.
assignedCard.boundary: The gap must fit the expected noise and response needs. A larger gap can hide a real change for longer, and retaining state is unsuitable when every threshold crossing must be acted on immediately.
assignedCard.source_fact: Texas Instruments' comparator reference circuit uses upper and lower thresholds to reduce undesirable transitions caused by noise or slowly changing signals.
assignedCard.source_note: Relation is an authored abstraction of the cited source, not a quotation. Boundary states limits on candidate transfer, not a tested product result.

actions.action: Replace chat updates with one pinned checkout record
actions.mechanism: A shared record separates the last confirmed holder from pending transfers, preventing newer conversation from obscuring custody.
actions.implementation: Pin an editable sheet accessible to both volunteers. Add timestamped handoff rows and a summary showing confirmed holder and unresolved transfers.
actions.check: Enter three completed handoffs among unrelated chat messages; both volunteers must identify the same holder using only the pinned record.
actions.risk: Manual summary edits can contradict the handoff rows.

j1.reason: A shared pinned record summarizes confirmed custody and unresolved transfers from timestamped handoff rows.

j2.reason: A pinned shared record with timestamped rows and a summary directly exposes confirmed holder and unresolved transfers.

actions.action: Require the receiving volunteer to confirm each handoff
actions.mechanism: A proposed transfer remains unresolved until its recipient acknowledges physical receipt; sending a message alone cannot establish custody.
actions.implementation: Record sender, recipient, and transfer time. Recipient confirms receipt and its time; only then update the confirmed holder. Block overlapping transfers.
actions.check: Propose a transfer without acknowledgment: it must remain unresolved and preserve the last confirmed holder. Acknowledgment must complete it.
actions.risk: Forgotten confirmation leaves actual custody uncertain despite a clear pending status.

j1.reason: The recipient must confirm physical receipt and its time before the recorded holder changes.

j2.reason: Recipient acknowledgment is required before changing the confirmed holder, with unresolved offers preserved and timed.

actions.action: Add a physical-possession reconciliation step
actions.mechanism: Explicit uncertainty prevents stale records from presenting a disputed holder as fact, while preserving unresolved handoff history.
actions.implementation: Before room use, either volunteer can flag a mismatch. Both check possession; record their timestamped responses and resolve custody without deleting prior entries.
actions.check: Simulate a recorded holder denying possession. The record must show custody unverified until the other volunteer confirms possession; retain the discrepancy.
actions.risk: If neither volunteer finds the key, reconciliation cannot establish a holder.

j1.reason: The two volunteers reconcile disputed possession through timestamped responses while preserving visible uncertainty and prior records.

j2.reason: A mismatch flag and timestamped responses expose disputed possession while preserving prior records until reconciliation.

actions.action: Require receipt confirmation before changing the recorded holder
actions.mechanism: Separate a proposed handoff from confirmed receipt; unanswered proposals remain visibly unresolved rather than silently transferring responsibility.
actions.implementation: Use a shared sheet accessible to both volunteers. Sender records recipient and handoff time; recipient confirms receipt and its time.
actions.check: Propose a transfer without confirmation: the previous confirmed holder remains shown alongside the unresolved transfer. Confirm receipt: the holder changes.
actions.risk: Recorded custody can lag reality; label it “last confirmed holder.”

j1.reason: A timestamped recipient confirmation changes the holder, while an unconfirmed proposal remains visibly unresolved.

j2.reason: The shared sheet separates a proposed handoff from recipient confirmation, leaving the prior confirmed holder visible until receipt.

actions.action: Preserve handoff history instead of overwriting it
actions.mechanism: An append-only handoff log preserves the sequence and makes corrections distinguishable from actual key movements.
actions.implementation: Give each handoff an ID. Record both volunteers, handoff time, and confirmation. Correct mistakes with timestamped entries referencing the original ID.
actions.check: Enter two transfers, then correct an erroneous time. Verify both transfers and the correction remain traceable without creating another transfer.
actions.risk: Manual editing can erase history; enable version history where available.

j1.reason: Timestamped corrections reference original handoffs, preserving an inspectable history rather than overwriting custody events.

j2.reason: An append-only log with handoff IDs and timestamped corrections preserves custody history instead of overwriting it.

actions.action: Pin one status view with an unresolved queue
actions.mechanism: A single authoritative summary separates confirmed custody from pending transfers, preventing scattered chat messages from competing as status reports.
actions.implementation: Pin the sheet link in chat. Show last confirmed holder, latest confirmed handoff time, and every unresolved handoff with its age.
actions.check: Create an unanswered handoff and add unrelated chat messages. Both volunteers must still locate the holder and pending handoff through the pin.
actions.risk: An outdated summary misleads; derive it from the log rather than copying.

j1.reason: A pinned summary exposes the last confirmed holder, handoff time, and unresolved transfers without searching chat.

j2.reason: One pinned status view with last confirmed holder and unresolved queue matches the authoritative key-status card mechanism.

actions.action: Require receipt confirmation before changing the holder
actions.mechanism: Separate a proposed transfer from confirmed receipt; unanswered requests remain visibly unresolved rather than silently changing ownership.
actions.implementation: Provide “Offer key” and “Received key” buttons for the two volunteers. Record offer time, actual handoff time, and confirmation time.
actions.check: Offer without acceptance: the last confirmed holder remains displayed beside a pending warning. Acceptance updates the holder and preserves handoff time.
actions.risk: An unconfirmed physical transfer makes the displayed holder provisional.

j1.reason: Offer and receipt are separate events, with actual handoff time preserved and custody changing only on acceptance.

j2.reason: Offer and receipt buttons keep proposed transfers pending until the recipient confirms and records the handoff time.

actions.action: Replace chat searching with one checkout summary
actions.mechanism: A single authoritative summary exposes the latest confirmed holder and every unresolved transfer without interpreting conversational messages.
actions.implementation: Pin a shared checkout page in chat. Generate its holder and unresolved-handoff sections from timestamped records; retain corrections instead of overwriting history.
actions.check: Record two completed transfers and one pending transfer. Verify the summary identifies the last confirmed holder and pending transfer without opening chat history.
actions.risk: Parallel informal records could undermine the authoritative summary.

j1.reason: A pinned page derives the confirmed holder and unresolved transfers from timestamped records rather than conversational messages.

j2.reason: A pinned summary derived from timestamped records identifies the last confirmed holder and unresolved handoffs without adding volunteers or hardware.

actions.action: Reconcile stalled or disputed handoffs explicitly
actions.mechanism: An unresolved transfer triggers a possession check, not an automatic reassignment based on elapsed time.
actions.implementation: Let the volunteers choose a reminder interval. On expiry, ask both who physically has the key; record agreement and actual handoff time.
actions.check: Leave a transfer unanswered past the interval: it remains unresolved. Conflicting replies show “holder disputed”; matching replies resolve it with a timestamped record.
actions.risk: Resolution still depends on volunteers responding accurately.

j1.reason: Expiry triggers a possession check, but agreement and a recorded handoff time—not elapsed time—resolve disputed custody.

j2.reason: Expired unresolved handoffs trigger explicit possession checking and a disputed state instead of automatic reassignment.

actions.action: Require acknowledgment before completing a key handoff
actions.mechanism: Separate proposed transfers from confirmed receipt, retaining the last confirmed holder while explicitly showing uncertainty.
actions.implementation: Give only the two volunteers access. Sender selects “Offer key”; recipient selects “Received” and records handoff time. Allow one pending transfer.
actions.check: Offer without acknowledgment: the display must show the last confirmed holder and unresolved transfer. Acknowledge: holder and handoff time must update.
actions.risk: An unrecorded physical transfer can still make the display stale.

j1.reason: Recipient acknowledgment and recorded handoff time gate custody changes while unanswered offers remain unresolved.

j2.reason: Access is limited to the two volunteers and custody changes only after acknowledged receipt with a handoff time.

actions.action: Replace chat searching with one pinned key record
actions.mechanism: An append-only handoff history supplies a single current summary without silently erasing disputed or corrected entries.
actions.implementation: Pin a shared record showing last confirmed holder, handoff time, and unresolved transfers. Record corrections as linked entries; regenerate the summary.
actions.check: Enter two completed transfers, then correct one timestamp. Verify the current holder remains correct and both timestamp versions remain inspectable.
actions.risk: Maintaining a separate chat-based record would recreate conflicting sources.

j1.reason: Linked corrections preserve both timestamp versions and regenerate custody status from an append-only history.

j2.reason: A pinned record showing last confirmed holder and unresolved transfers is the same authoritative status-card mechanism with append-only history support.

actions.action: Escalate overdue handoffs into explicit reconciliation
actions.mechanism: A deadline surfaces missing acknowledgment without automatically treating silence as receipt or cancellation.
actions.implementation: Have the volunteers choose an acknowledgment window. Flag overdue transfers and notify both. Resolve through timestamped receipt, sender-confirmed non-transfer, or an explicit dispute.
actions.check: Let an offer expire. Verify it remains unresolved, both volunteers are notified, and no holder change occurs solely from elapsed time.
actions.risk: Reminders cannot establish physical possession when volunteers disagree.

j1.reason: An acknowledgment deadline prompts both volunteers without changing custody automatically and offers explicit resolution paths.

j2.reason: An acknowledgment window with notifications surfaces unresolved handoffs while preserving custody until a timestamped resolution.

actions.action: Require the recipient to confirm receipt
actions.mechanism: Separate intended transfers from acknowledged possession so an offer never silently changes the holder.
actions.implementation: Create a pending handoff when the sender offers the key. On receipt, the other volunteer confirms and records the actual handoff time.
actions.check: Offer a transfer without confirming it. Verify the last confirmed holder remains labeled and the handoff stays unresolved until receipt.
actions.risk: Forgotten confirmations leave physical possession uncertain.

actions.action: Offer a paper ledger as a digital alternative
actions.mechanism: A fixed, shared ledger provides inspectable custody records without hardware, accounts, or reliance on chat access.
actions.implementation: Instead of the digital workflow, keep a ledger somewhere both can access without the key. Record each handoff's time, names, and both initials.
actions.check: Leave a transfer row missing recipient initials. Verify either volunteer can identify the last jointly confirmed holder and unresolved transfer.
actions.risk: Requires visiting the ledger; missing entries remain possible.

actions.action: Remind volunteers about unresolved handoffs
actions.mechanism: Age-based prompts draw attention to incomplete transfers without silently declaring that custody changed.
actions.implementation: Choose a reminder interval together. Notify the recipient of pending receipt confirmation and keep the unresolved item pinned for both volunteers.
actions.check: Leave a test handoff pending beyond the interval. Verify a reminder appears, custody stays unchanged, and confirmation stops further prompts.
actions.risk: Frequent reminders can become background noise.

actions.action: Show one authoritative key-status card
actions.mechanism: A stable summary exposes possession and outstanding transfers without requiring volunteers to reconstruct the conversation.
actions.implementation: Pin a shared status view showing last confirmed holder, confirmation time, and every unresolved handoff. Label pending transfers prominently rather than implying certain possession.
actions.check: After confirmed, pending, and disputed transfers, verify the card matches the records and identifies unresolved items without opening chat history.
actions.risk: A stale cached view can mislead readers.

actions.action: Keep a timestamped, append-only handoff history
actions.mechanism: Preserved events make custody changes reconstructable without searching conversational messages or trusting an overwritten status.
actions.implementation: Record sender, recipient, physical handoff time, and submission time. Require handoff time on confirmation; append corrections rather than deleting entries.
actions.check: Enter a delayed confirmation, then correct its time. Verify both versions remain and the latest valid custody state is displayed.
actions.risk: Volunteer-entered physical times may be approximate.

actions.action: Add an explicit custody-dispute recovery path
actions.mechanism: An uncertainty state exposes conflicting reports instead of presenting the last recorded holder as verified physical possession.
actions.implementation: Let either volunteer flag uncertainty. Preserve the last confirmed holder; require a named possession claim and the other's acknowledgment to resolve it.
actions.check: Flag conflicting possession reports. Verify uncertainty stays visible until both volunteers acknowledge the same resolution, with its time recorded.
actions.risk: Resolution stalls when either volunteer cannot respond.

actions.action: Provide an explicit possession-dispute workflow
actions.mechanism: Represent uncertainty directly instead of choosing whichever volunteer edited the record most recently.
actions.implementation: Let either volunteer flag incorrect possession. Preserve the last confirmed holder; show current possession as disputed. Resolve through both volunteers acknowledging a correction and its effective time.
actions.check: Submit contradictory possession reports. Verify uncertainty remains visible until both acknowledge a resolution and the original reports remain inspectable.
actions.risk: Resolution stalls when either volunteer is unavailable.

actions.action: Reject conflicting or repeated transfer submissions
actions.mechanism: Version checks and unique request identifiers prevent concurrent edits and retries from corrupting custody state.
actions.implementation: Accept a transfer only against the latest record version; allow one active transfer. Treat retries with the same identifier as the original submission.
actions.check: Submit conflicting transfers simultaneously, then repeat one request. Verify only one transfer exists and the rejected volunteer receives the current state.
actions.risk: Offline submissions may require review before acceptance.

actions.action: Separate future arrangements from actual possession
actions.mechanism: Plans and reservations cannot overwrite custody, preventing statements such as 'I'll take it tomorrow' from becoming false location information.
actions.implementation: Add a separate Planned handoff section with intended participants and scheduled time. Require the ordinary receipt-confirmation process for actual transfer.
actions.check: Schedule tomorrow's transfer and let its scheduled time pass. Verify current custody remains unchanged and no completed handoff is fabricated.
actions.risk: Volunteers may mistake scheduling for completing the transfer.

actions.action: Reject conflicting or repeated transfers
actions.mechanism: Version checks and unique transfer identifiers prevent stale screens or repeated taps from producing contradictory custody records.
actions.implementation: Allow one pending transfer. Atomically validate the current holder and record version; process each confirmation identifier only once.
actions.check: Submit competing offers from stale screens, then repeat a confirmation. Verify one transfer survives and custody changes only once.
actions.risk: Rejected submissions need clear refresh instructions.

actions.action: Require receipt confirmation before changing the holder
actions.mechanism: A proposed handoff stays unresolved until the receiving volunteer confirms possession; intent does not establish custody.
actions.implementation: Provide Offer and Confirm receipt buttons in one shared record. Display last confirmed holder, intended recipient, and pending status.
actions.check: Offer a transfer without confirming it. Verify the holder remains unchanged and the unresolved handoff is visible.
actions.risk: Forgotten confirmation leaves physical possession uncertain.

actions.action: Remind volunteers about unfinished handoffs
actions.mechanism: Age-based prompts surface forgotten confirmations without treating elapsed time as evidence that the key moved.
actions.implementation: Let the two volunteers choose a reminder interval. Prompt both when a handoff remains pending; offer confirm receipt, cancel an uncompleted transfer, or dispute.
actions.check: Leave a test handoff pending beyond the interval. Verify a reminder appears, ownership remains unchanged, and resolution stops further reminders.
actions.risk: Frequent reminders may be ignored or muted.

actions.action: Record handoffs in an append-only history
actions.mechanism: Structured records replace scattered chat messages while preserving earlier entries and corrections.
actions.implementation: For each handoff, save sender, recipient, handoff time, submission time, and status. Restrict participants to the two existing volunteers; corrections reference earlier records.
actions.check: Record two handoffs and correct one timestamp. Verify both originals remain visible and the corrected time is clearly identified.
actions.risk: Entered handoff times depend on volunteer accuracy.

task.title: Development: source-bound glossary
task.brief: An editor maintains definitions linked to supplied source passages. A definition may be disputed.
constraints: Every definition needs a source passage ID.
success_criteria: A reader can inspect the source and disagreement.

assignedCard.label: Prescribed fire management
assignedCard.relation: Accumulated material can increase the scale of a later uncontrolled disruption. A planned bounded intervention removes some of that material while predefined conditions permit control. Monitoring continues during the intervention; if the conditions are unsuitable, a different removal method is used.
assignedCard.boundary: The intervention is not automatically beneficial. It needs a limited scope, a go/no-go condition, monitoring, and a feasible alternative. Do not transfer intentional destruction to irreplaceable target material.
assignedCard.source_fact: NPS uses prescribed burns and other fuel treatments under management plans and go/no-go conditions; mechanical removal can be used when burning is not appropriate.
assignedCard.source_note: Relation is an authored abstraction of the cited source, not a quotation. Boundary states limits on candidate transfer, not a tested product result.

actions.action: Require passage-backed definitions before saving.
actions.mechanism: A required passage reference binds each definition to the supplied material and blocks dangling citations.
actions.implementation: Import supplied passages with immutable IDs. Require every definition variant to reference an existing passage ID; reject unknown IDs and external-source references.
actions.check: Attempt saves with missing, unknown, and valid passage IDs. Only the valid reference succeeds; deleting its passage is blocked.
actions.risk: A valid reference does not establish that wording is supported.

j1.reason: Required supplied-passage references and deletion protection enforce source attachment with observable save tests.

j2.reason: It blocks dangling and external references by requiring every definition variant to cite an imported supplied passage ID.

actions.action: Keep competing definitions as separate variants.
actions.mechanism: Variant records preserve disagreement without forcing an editor to overwrite or merge competing wording.
actions.implementation: Store each wording under the same term with its own ID and required passage ID. Record disputes between variants, including reasons; retain superseded wording.
actions.check: Enter two conflicting definitions, then revise one. Both original wordings, their passage links, and the dispute remain inspectable.
actions.risk: Numerous variants can obscure the disagreement without clear labels.

j1.reason: Independently sourced variant records prevent competing definitions from being overwritten and test preservation after revision.

j2.reason: It preserves competing wording as separate sourced records with disputes rather than overwriting or merging definitions.

actions.action: Show definitions, passages, and disputes together.
actions.mechanism: An expandable comparison view lets readers inspect competing wording against its cited passages without losing context.
actions.implementation: Add a source-and-disagreement control to each definition. Display the full referenced passage, passage ID, competing variants, and recorded dispute reasons; support keyboard navigation.
actions.check: Starting from either disputed variant, verify a reader can open its source and reach every linked competing wording using only the keyboard.
actions.risk: Long passages may require scrolling; excerpts alone can conceal context.

j1.reason: A keyboard-accessible inspection control exposes full passages, competing wording, and dispute reasons together.

j2.reason: It combines definitions, passages, passage IDs, and disputes in an expandable inspection control with an observable keyboard check.

actions.action: Review wording changes against their cited passages.
actions.mechanism: A review queue separates citation existence from editorial judgments about whether the passage supports the definition.
actions.implementation: Queue new and revised variants for passage-only review. Record supported, disputed, or pending status with reasons; retain wording and passage IDs regardless of judgment.
actions.check: Revise a reviewed definition. Confirm its new revision becomes pending while the previous wording and review remain available.
actions.risk: Review labels reflect editorial judgments, not independent verification.

j1.reason: Passage-only editorial review evaluates wording support separately from citation validity while retaining earlier wording and judgments.

j2.reason: It adds a review status for whether cited supplied passages support wording while retaining all wording and passage IDs.

actions.action: Require valid source links before saving definitions
actions.mechanism: A required reference to an existing supplied passage prevents definitions from becoming detached from their evidence.
actions.implementation: Store passage IDs in a supplied-source registry. Require each definition variant to reference an existing ID; prohibit deleting referenced passages.
actions.check: Attempt saves with missing, unknown, and valid IDs. Only the valid case succeeds, and its source link opens the referenced passage.
actions.risk: A valid reference does not establish that wording is supported.

j1.reason: A supplied-source registry, mandatory valid references, and deletion restrictions enforce persistent source attachment.

j2.reason: It enforces existing supplied passage IDs for each definition variant and tests missing, unknown, and valid references.

actions.action: Display competing wording beside its source
actions.mechanism: Separate variants preserve disagreement without forcing disputed definitions into a single editorial formulation.
actions.implementation: Give each variant its own wording, passage ID, and stable ID. Add a comparison view showing variants, source passages, and recorded objections.
actions.check: Enter two conflicting definitions. Verify readers can inspect both wordings, each source, and the objection without accessing editor-only controls.
actions.risk: An editorial preference could visually overshadow alternatives; label preference explicitly.

j1.reason: The comparison view exposes preserved variants, their supplied passages, and objections without editor-only access.

j2.reason: It shows each variant, its passage ID, source passage, and objection in a reader-accessible comparison view.

actions.action: Review source changes without silently replacing evidence
actions.mechanism: Versioned passages retain original support while dependency checks identify definitions needing review after a source edit.
actions.implementation: Assign changed passages new IDs and link their predecessors. Flag dependent variants for review; retain their original wording and references until explicitly revised.
actions.check: Edit a passage supporting two variants. Both receive review flags; their original passages remain inspectable, and neither reference changes automatically.
actions.risk: Review flags may accumulate; they must not hide existing definitions.

j1.reason: New passage versions trigger dependent-definition review without silently changing original wording or evidence bindings.

j2.reason: It prevents silent rebinding after passage edits by assigning new IDs and preserving original wording and references.

actions.action: Make competing wording searchable and directly shareable
actions.mechanism: Indexing every variant lets readers discover disagreements even when their search uses wording absent from the preferred definition.
actions.implementation: Index all variant text and passage IDs locally. Return term-grouped results with matched wording, dispute indicators, and stable links to individual variants.
actions.check: Search a phrase unique to a nonpreferred variant. Its result appears, and its direct link exposes that wording, source, and competing definition.
actions.risk: Grouping must not conceal which variant actually matched the query.

j1.reason: Indexing every variant prevents preferred wording from hiding alternatives and tests retrieval using a nonpreferred phrase.

j2.reason: It indexes all variant wording and exposes matched variants, disputes, and passage IDs in search results.

actions.action: Require valid passage links before saving definitions
actions.mechanism: Referential integrity prevents definitions from becoming detached from the supplied evidence.
actions.implementation: Store supplied passages by immutable ID. Require each definition variant to reference an existing passage; reject missing or unknown IDs.
actions.check: Attempt saves with missing, unknown, and valid passage IDs. Only the valid case must succeed and resolve to its passage.
actions.risk: A valid link does not establish that the passage supports the wording.

j1.reason: Rejecting missing or unknown supplied-passage IDs enforces the required source binding for every variant.

j2.reason: It requires each definition variant to reference an existing supplied passage and rejects missing or unknown IDs.

actions.action: Show competing wording beside its evidence
actions.mechanism: An explicit dispute view exposes alternatives without merging their wording or implying consensus.
actions.implementation: Group variants under a term. Display each wording, passage ID, expandable source passage, and recorded objection; label editorial preference separately.
actions.check: Create two conflicting variants. A reader must access both exact wordings, their passages, and the objection from the term view.
actions.risk: Visual ordering can imply endorsement; label ordering and preference explicitly.

j1.reason: The term view preserves competing wording and exposes each passage and objection for reader inspection.

j2.reason: It exposes exact competing wordings, passage IDs, expandable supplied passages, and objections from the term view.

actions.action: Flag definitions affected by source corrections
actions.mechanism: Versioned passages preserve historical evidence while dependency tracking identifies definitions needing renewed review.
actions.implementation: Give corrected supplied passages new IDs linked to predecessors. Preserve original links and wording; mark dependent definitions for review without automatically rebinding them.
actions.check: Correct one passage. Only its dependent definitions must be flagged; their original wording and cited passage must remain inspectable.
actions.risk: Repeated corrections can accumulate unresolved review flags.

j1.reason: Versioned source corrections preserve original evidence and flag only dependent definitions for renewed review.

j2.reason: It versions corrected supplied passages, keeps original links, and flags dependent definitions for review.

actions.action: Review disputed terms in bounded batches
actions.mechanism: Limited review scope and explicit stop conditions constrain accidental loss while retaining unresolved alternatives.
actions.implementation: Select five disputed terms. Start only when cited passages resolve; record proposed decisions without overwriting variants. Stop on missing evidence; retain individual review instead.
actions.check: Interrupt a batch after two decisions. All competing wording and links must survive; untouched terms must remain unresolved.
actions.risk: Batch decisions may flatten distinct objections; require a rationale per term.

j1.reason: A bounded review workflow uses evidence prerequisites and stop conditions while testing that interruptions preserve alternatives.

j2.reason: It limits dispute review to bounded batches, records rationales without overwriting variants, and preserves links.

actions.action: Require valid passage links before saving definitions
actions.mechanism: Local referential integrity prevents definitions from becoming detached from the supplied source material.
actions.implementation: Store supplied passages under stable IDs. Require each definition to reference at least one existing passage ID; reject missing or unknown IDs.
actions.check: Attempt saves with absent, unknown, and valid IDs. Only valid references should save, and each should open its exact passage.
actions.risk: A valid link does not establish that the passage supports the wording.

j1.reason: Required existing supplied-passage IDs prevent unsourced saves and provide a directly testable reference check.

j2.reason: It uses local referential integrity so definitions cannot save without an existing supplied passage ID.

actions.action: Show competing wording beside its source
actions.mechanism: An explicit disagreement view makes alternatives inspectable without collapsing them into a single preferred definition.
actions.implementation: Give each competing definition its own record and passage IDs. Display alternatives side by side with expandable passages and source-linked dispute notes.
actions.check: Create two conflicting definitions. Verify a reader can inspect both complete wordings, their passages, and the stated disagreement without editor permissions.
actions.risk: Visual prominence can imply endorsement; label editorial preference explicitly.

j1.reason: Side-by-side alternatives with expandable supplied passages make preserved wording and disagreement inspectable by readers.

j2.reason: It provides a reader-facing view of competing wording, source passage IDs, full passages, and dispute notes.

actions.action: Preserve edits as inspectable definition revisions
actions.mechanism: Append-only revisions retain earlier wording and source bindings instead of silently replacing disputed material.
actions.implementation: Make edits create revisions containing wording, passage IDs, author, and change reason. Keep competing alternatives separate; expose revision history and restoration.
actions.check: Revise and restore a disputed definition. Confirm every revision retains resolvable passage IDs and that neither operation removes the competing alternative.
actions.risk: Revision history can become noisy; distinguish chronological edits from competing interpretations.

j1.reason: Append-only edits preserve wording and passage bindings while keeping competing interpretations separate from chronological revisions.

j2.reason: It makes edits append-only revisions that retain wording and passage IDs while distinguishing alternatives.

actions.action: Review disputed entries in bounded batches
actions.mechanism: A small review scope and explicit stop conditions limit accidental loss during accumulated dispute cleanup.
actions.implementation: Review five entries per batch only when all passage links resolve. Monitor retained alternatives; stop on missing wording or links and switch to annotation-only review.
actions.check: Seed a batch with a broken link. Verify cleanup stops, all wording survives, and annotation-only review remains available.
actions.risk: Triage can postpone difficult disagreements; keep unresolved entries visibly queued.

j1.reason: Small review batches stop on missing evidence or wording and test preservation through an annotation-only fallback.

j2.reason: It proposes an operational batch-review workflow that preserves wording and links and stops on missing evidence.

actions.action: Show the source beside each definition
actions.mechanism: An inline source viewer lets readers inspect evidence without losing their place in the glossary.
actions.implementation: Add a source button displaying the linked passage ID and exact supplied text beside the definition; support keyboard opening and closing.
actions.check: Open every definition’s source button and compare displayed text with its stored passage. Verify keyboard focus returns correctly.
actions.risk: Long passages can overwhelm the reading layout.

actions.action: Require valid source links before saving definitions
actions.mechanism: Enforce source attachment in storage, so neither editor forms nor imports can create ungrounded definitions.
actions.implementation: Require each definition to reference at least one existing supplied passage ID. Reject missing references and restrict deletion of referenced passages.
